Adversarially review the diff at /Users/elmabi/Desktop/my-projets/workstation on branch chantier/rail-en-production-et-juge-honnete
vs base "main" (run `git -C /Users/elmabi/Desktop/my-projets/workstation diff main...HEAD` to see it — 12 files, ~1200 insertions / 102 deletions,
5 commits). This branch fixes two production incidents in a workstation "banc d'essai" (skill-improvement
rail): (1) an import marker that permanently sealed a recoverable failure (server/cli/evalsReconciler.ts,
RETRYABLE_ON_FAILURE_KINDS), (2) a provenance-check false positive in a local LLM judge that rejected honest
citations due to JSON escaping + typographic punctuation (server/services/reviews/localJudge.ts,
normalizeForProvenance / decodeJsonlStringValues), plus two follow-up chip fixes: (3) a git-merge
"unrelated histories" failure when applying skill-improvement branches, fixed by a hand-built two-parent
merge commit that mechanically confines its tree diff to <skill>/ (server/services/reviews/apply.ts,
graftSkillContent — uses raw git plumbing: rm -r, checkout, write-tree, commit-tree), and (4) two race
conditions in a CLI "wait for a hub conversation to be answered" command (server/cli/convo.ts, wakeReason —
removed a stale baseline-comparison mechanism in favor of a pure function of the current snapshot). Docs
were updated in docs/evals/*.md and docs/decision-hub.md to match.
Read the full changed files + their callers/siblings, AND read the MOST-BOUNDED/safest sibling of any
git-plumbing call, marker/lock pattern, or CLI exit-code contract you touch, so you know THIS repo's idiom.
For any file/function that is WHOLLY NEW in this diff (e.g. graftSkillContent, decodeJsonlStringValues,
RETRYABLE_ON_FAILURE_KINDS), audit it standalone — there is no old behavior to diff against. For a
pre-existing function changed by this diff (wakeReason, normalizeForProvenance, mergeApprovedBranchIntoMain,
cmdImport's catch block), scope to what the diff changed vs main, but verify the new behavior against EVERY
call site and EVERY code path (success AND failure) of that function, not just the one path the commit
message describes.
A finding is reportable if it fails ANY gate:
  • CORRECTNESS: some input makes it wrong / crash / lose data (triggerable), OR
  • CONVENTION/SCALABILITY/PLATFORM-LIMIT: it deviates from an idiom that ALREADY exists in this repo
    (cite the sibling file:line that does it right), violates an external hard limit, or is an unbounded
    read / full-table scan / N+1 / over-fetch — EVEN IF today's data makes it work.
  • WIRING: new/changed enforcement/tooling code (marker files that gate at-most-once application, a
    provenance security check, a git-merge safety boundary, a CLI exit-code contract) that does not
    actually fire against this repo's real data shapes/paths, or is not wired into every place the same
    invariant should hold (e.g. is the graft's path-safety guard checked BEFORE every destructive git
    call, not just the first one? does the marker-retry logic apply to every code path that can throw?).
  • STATE-SAFETY: a gate/marker/lock that can be satisfied without the protected work happening, that can
    be bypassed by a crafted input (e.g. a skill name, a candidate id), that leaves the repo/data in a
    half-mutated state on a mid-operation crash, or that can block forever (no escape hatch / re-entrancy
    guard). This is CENTRAL to this diff: it is exactly the class of bug (a marker/gate posed before a
    side-effect, never retired on failure) that motivated the whole chantier — verify the NEW code doesn't
    reintroduce a narrower version of the SAME defect it fixes (e.g. does graftSkillContent's git plumbing
    leave the integration clone in a half-reset state on a partial failure? does the new judge-local-adjacent
    change interact badly with the STILL-UNFIXED judge-local-markers "judging" stuck-state defect, already
    flagged as a separate known chip?).
"Returns correct output today / not triggerable" is NOT grounds to drop a convention/scalability/
platform-limit/wiring/state-safety finding — those are precisely what a review bot flags. Refute
ONLY pure style (naming/formatting/taste/restated guards).

DIMENSION: Exit-code contract of convo watch (0/1/2) truly unchanged in every branch? Behavior/parity vs the code each function replaces (old wakeReason vs new, old merge vs graft) — any silent behavior change not covered by a test? Any unverified behavioral CLAIM in a comment or doc that the code does not structurally guarantee (e.g. claims about what git commit-tree produces, claims about JSONL escaping)?

If a finding overlaps another dimension's territory, note the overlap in one line rather than re-developing it.
